card.name: Qualifying turn after a limiting statement
card.fires_on: Small words like only, but, though, although, simply and is that come right after a negated or limited claim and introduce a softer or partial counterpoint. They appear in sentences such as 'X cannot do A, but it can do B'.

modes.label: Contrast word after a negation
modes.description: But, although or though follows a clause saying something is not enough, not complete or uncommon, and brings in a mitigating point.
modes.example: It does not list every paper ever published,<< but>> it is still an excellent list.

modes.label: Narrowing word after can or cannot
modes.description: Only, simply or a verb right after it limits what something can do to a smaller effect.
modes.example: they can<< only>> make them somewhat less dangerous.

card.plain: It marks the spot where a sentence admits a limit and then turns to a smaller, qualified point.
evidence: they can<< only>> make them somewhat less dangerous.
